subject: dsa
title: Regular Expression Matching
summary: dp[i][j] is true when s's first i chars match p's first j chars. A normal char matches when letters are equal or the pattern is a dot; a star either drops its preceding char or, when that char matches, consumes one char of s.
problem: Decide whether s = "aa" matches pattern p = "a*", where '.' matches any char and '*' means zero or more of the preceding char. Rows are prefixes of s ("", a, aa); columns are prefixes of p ("", a, *). dp[i][j] is true when s's first i chars match p's first j chars.

steps.caption: Rows are s "aa", columns are p "a*". A star means zero or more of the char before it. Empty matches empty, so dp[0][0] is T.
Base row 0 is the empty s. Pattern "a*" can match empty by taking zero a's, so dp[0][2] is T while dp[0][1] is F.
Row a: dp[1][1] is T since a matches a, and dp[1][2] is T since a* consumes one a from s.
Row aa: dp[2][1] is F because a alone cannot match aa, but dp[2][2] is T since a* consumes the second a.
The bottom-right cell dp[2][2] is T, so "aa" matches the pattern "a*".
